subject: High error rate and sustained qps shortfall on reserved pool — StrandPay

From: Jill Park <jill.park@strandpay.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate: increasing 503s and latency on reserved pool (StrandPay)

Hi Marcus / Aditya,

We started seeing a sustained jump in 5xx (mainly 503) errors on our reserved capacity around 08:45 PT — roughly +18% 5xx rate and p95 latency for text-generation spiked from 420ms to ~1.7s. Traffic pattern hasn't changed on our side (same qps and prompt sizes). This is impacting checkout flows for a subset of customers.

Quick facts:
- Window: 08:45–09:05 PT
- Avg QPS: 120 (reserved pool)
- 5xx rate: baseline 0.4% -> current 18%
- Errors: mostly 503 gateway and occasional token-queue OOMs

I attached a small error sample and a screenshot of the dashboard — we also pasted the top of the stack trace in the attachment kvcache-sample.txt. Can you confirm whether this is a capacity saturation, kernel regression, or something in the KV cache layer? We need an ETA for mitigation or a short-term fallback plan (smaller model, lower concurrency, or burst capacity).

Our procurement and CTO want a clear readout; this will need exec visibility if we can't stabilize in the next hour.

--
Jill Park
Head of Platform Reliability, StrandPay
jill.park@strandpay.com

Attachments: error-sample-logs.txt, screenshot-503s.png, kvcache-sample.txt

Folks — tagging this as P0.

Jill, thanks for the quick signal and the attachments. I'm on it. Initial thoughts: looks like saturation on one of the dedicated GPU slices backing StrandPay's reserved reservation; the token-queue OOM hints at a KV cache or batching bottleneck rather than pure infra loss.

Immediate asks:
- Vivek: can you stand up an exec bridge and authorize burst capacity for the next 2 hours if needed? Customer is explicitly asking for CEO/CTO visibility.
- Neha: can you pull per-host kernel metrics (cpu/gpu util, memory alloc, queue depth, kv cache hit ratio) for the last 30m and share top error traces? Prioritize hosts that serve their model id: rwd-gpt-large-v1.
- Aditya: please pre-draft a short customer note (2–3 bullets) explaining the rollback/fallback options (model downshift, concurrency cap, short burst).

I'll start a short triage doc in the linked Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3218 and add logs from the attachments.

We should assume a fallback plan if metrics don't stabilize in 20 minutes.

Thanks — Marcus
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Logging summary (first-pass diagnostics):
- Hosts impacted: pool-rwd-usw2-32a, -32b, -32c (shard 14).
- GPU util: 79-92% on the three hosts (sustained), kernel context-switch spikes coincident with increased queue depth.
- KV cache: hit ratio dropped from 87% -> 62% in the 08:40–09:00 window (evictions increased).
- Batching: observed larger-than-usual prefix batching for a small subset of requests which inflated token growth due to a client-side pattern of long system prompts.
- Errors: 503 gateway emitted after token-queue reach threshold and several OOMs when prewarming failed.

Immediate recommended actions (short-term):
1) Authorize Vivek's burst into shared pool for 60–120 minutes (reduces immediate 5xx).
2) Apply a temporary concurrency cap on StrandPay's critical routes to 60 qps per shard (we can step down gradually).
3) Push a short-lived model fallback to rwd-gpt-medium for their high-variance endpoints; this reduces per-token memory pressure.
4) Post-incident: we need to increase KV cache capacity for that reservation slice + add an autoscale rule for queue depth > 75%.

I've attached the small kvcache dump and a trimmed trace in error-sample-logs.txt. If we go with the burst + concurrency cap approach I can run the roll-forward now.

-Neha
Senior SRE, Serving Platform
Redwood Inference
